top_choice_rationale: P003 awards the optical lattice clock alone to Katori and Ye. Katori's magic-wavelength lattice is a genuine atomic-structure idea that removes the Doppler/recoil versus signal-to-noise trade-off, and Ye's group demonstrated its capability. The 10^-18 level has been reproduced and compared across independent laboratories, so the result rests on measurement and not interpretation. The two credits are complementary and separable, and the citation scope (the lattice clock as a step beyond the 2005 combs and 2012 single-ion control) is clean. P002 keeps the same part but adds IceCube, a pairing of unrelated achievements with unresolved credit for one name; P001 is a major new field but ranked below on maturity of consequences and my own assessment, and any award is preferred to none.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented connection to Katori or Ye, though my attosecond and storage-ring collaborations (L'Huillier, Keller, Schuch, Indelicato) are in neighbouring areas of atomic physics
